_metadata.description: WellaPath Adaptive Question Flow CANDIDATE — the first versioned representation of a flow that currently exists only as Dart source. Not published, not clinically approved, not consumed by any build.

vocabulary_2_0.note: W3 branching resolves canonical token IDs from token_dictionary 1.1 only. No alias, association or other Vocabulary 2.0 metadata participates in question eligibility.

impedance_mismatches.baseline_behaviour: Severity and duration questions are chosen by `severityQuestion ??= question` / `durationQuestion ??= question` while iterating the SELECTED symptom tokens, so which wording is asked depends on the order the user tapped symptoms.
impedance_mismatches.candidate_behaviour: Selection is by the declared order key (priority, tie_break_key, question_id), with tie_break_key = the trigger token id. The same symptom set always yields the same question regardless of selection order.
impedance_mismatches.why_it_exists: The current code has no tie-break at all; first-wins over an unordered user selection is the de-facto rule. W3 forbids ordering that depends on unstable iteration, and a tie with no declared resolution is a validation failure under this contract.
impedance_mismatches.affected_existing_paths: Only paths where two or more selected tokens each offer the same question type. The competing questions differ ONLY in wording (e.g. 'How severe is your headache?' vs 'How severe is this pain?'); the question type, answer options and produced tokens are identical.
required_mobile_tests: same symptom set selected in different orders yields an identical question sequence
order key is used for sorting; no reliance on List.sort stability or map iteration
regression evidence enumerating every path whose asked wording changes
impedance_mismatches.required_review: product — confirm the deterministically chosen wording is the right one on each changed tie path
impedance_mismatches.activation_blocker_reason: Production activation requires regression evidence showing every changed tie path.

impedance_mismatches.baseline_behaviour: Answers accumulate in a local map and `_commitAnswers()` runs only when the LAST follow-up question is answered, immediately before navigating to LoadingScreen. A red-flag clarifier 'yes' does not interrupt; the red flag is evaluated once, in the engine, after every follow-up question has been presented.
impedance_mismatches.candidate_behaviour: Every red-flag-affecting question declares evaluate_after_answer=true and blocks_next_question=true, requiring evaluation immediately after that answer and before the next ordinary question or scoring.
impedance_mismatches.why_it_exists: The locked architecture states red flags run before scoring and override it. The current implementation satisfies that for the ENGINE but not for the QUESTION FLOW: the user keeps answering ordinary questions after declaring a danger sign. Recorded as defect QB-002.
impedance_mismatches.affected_existing_paths: Any path where a red-flag clarifier is raised and answered 'Yes' while further follow-up questions remain. With 3 clarifiers and a 5-question limit, up to 4 further questions can be presented after the danger sign is declared.
impedance_mismatches.safety_direction: STRICTLY EARLIER, NEVER LATER. It cannot suppress a red flag that fires today; it fires the same red flag sooner. No red-flag token, rule or trigger is added or changed.
required_mobile_tests: clarifier answered Yes mid-sequence interrupts immediately; no further ordinary question is presented
scoring never runs before red-flag evaluation on that path
an ordinary (no red flag) path presents exactly the same questions as today
evaluation also runs after an edit and after restored state
telemetry cannot distinguish a red-flag path from an ordinary one
impedance_mismatches.required_review: engineering lead + clinical — behaviour change, clinically safe direction
impedance_mismatches.activation_blocker_reason: Adopted as a required safety correction and sequenced FIRST, ahead of the rest of the adaptive engine.

impedance_mismatches.area: adaptive re-branching on newly derived tokens
impedance_mismatches.baseline_behaviour: `_questions` is computed once in initState from the symptom set selected before the screen opened. A token added by an additionalSymptoms answer generates no further questions in the same assessment.
impedance_mismatches.candidate_behaviour: trigger_condition is re-evaluated against current state, so a token derived from an answer can make a further question eligible.
impedance_mismatches.why_it_exists: A flow that cannot react to its own answers is not adaptive. W3 requires conditional follow-up questions.
impedance_mismatches.affected_existing_paths: 56 (source-token, option-token) pairs where an additionalSymptoms option is itself a key in kFollowupQuestionMap. Newly triggerable: 11 severity, 54 duration and 56 additionalSymptoms questions. Bounded by the 5-question limit.
impedance_mismatches.changes_token_output: INDIRECTLY YES — measured, not assumed. Newly triggerable severity and duration questions produce tokens that carry NO kb scoring weight and are NOT red-flag relevant (verified: mild/moderate/severe/very_severe and days_1_3/days_3_7/days_7_plus/weeks_2_plus appear in neither kb symptoms nor rules). But newly triggerable additionalSymptoms questions DO affect scoring: they give the user further opportunities to declare symptoms, which can change the final token set and therefore the score and top condition.
impedance_mismatches.changes_red_flag_content: NO — verified: not one additionalSymptoms option anywhere in the map is a red-flag clarifier trigger token, so re-branching cannot raise a clarifier that does not fire today.
required_mobile_tests: re-branching is bounded by the path limit and cannot loop
a newly derived token never raises a red-flag clarifier that the baseline would not have raised
an assessment with no additionalSymptoms answer presents exactly the baseline questions
impedance_mismatches.required_review: product + clinical — this can change which symptoms a user ends up declaring, and therefore the score and top condition. It is a path change, not a content change: no question, answer meaning or token effect differs.
impedance_mismatches.activation_blocker_reason: Can change scoring inputs. Not required for the IM-002 safety correction and must not ship with it.

impedance_mismatches.baseline_behaviour: Answers are held in `Map<int, dynamic> _answers` keyed by the question's index in the list built at initState, and are meaningful only against that exact list.
impedance_mismatches.candidate_behaviour: Answers are keyed by stable question_id and answer_option_id.
impedance_mismatches.why_it_exists: Dependency-based invalidation, restoration and editing all require an answer to be identifiable independently of list position. An index cannot survive a list that changes.
impedance_mismatches.affected_existing_paths: None observable. Every path presents the same questions with the same answers; only the internal key changes.
required_mobile_tests: an answer survives a change to the question list without being reattributed to a different question
restoring state rebuilds answers by id, not by position
impedance_mismatches.activation_blocker_reason: Prerequisite for IM-002 edit/restore handling; no user-visible effect.

impedance_mismatches.baseline_behaviour: `result.length > 5 ? result.sublist(0, 5) : result` truncates the whole list after clarifiers are prepended. No clarifier is dropped today ONLY because there are 3 of them and they sort first.
impedance_mismatches.candidate_behaviour: red_flag_questions_exempt_from_truncation is a schema constant `true`. A red-flag-affecting question is never dropped to satisfy a length limit; if red-flag questions alone exceed the limit, the limit yields.
impedance_mismatches.why_it_exists: An incidental safety property is not a safety property. A fourth clarifier firing alongside others could push a red-flag question out of the list under the baseline rule.
impedance_mismatches.affected_existing_paths: None on today's data — with 3 clarifiers and a limit of 5 the two rules produce identical output on every one of the 2,325 explored paths. The difference is latent, not observable now.
required_mobile_tests: a synthetic set of 6 red-flag questions is presented in full rather than truncated to the limit
ordinary questions are the only ones dropped when the limit binds
impedance_mismatches.required_review: none — makes an existing incidental property structural
impedance_mismatches.activation_blocker_reason: Same observable behaviour on current data.

impedance_mismatches.baseline_behaviour: Sex, age, pregnancy, medical conditions and body area are separate Flutter screens with hardcoded navigation, not entries in any question list. The pregnancy gate is the getter `shouldShowPregnancyScreen => _sex == 'female'`.
impedance_mismatches.candidate_behaviour: Each is a question with a trigger_condition and a priority, so the whole flow is one ordered graph. The pregnancy gate is projected as {"sex": "female"} — the same predicate.
impedance_mismatches.why_it_exists: Path-length control, editing and invalidation cannot reason about a flow that is half data and half hardcoded navigation.
impedance_mismatches.affected_existing_paths: None. Verified: the pregnancy gate is true for female, false for male, and false for unknown — exactly the getter. Age and medical-condition token mappings are copied verbatim; body area produces no token, as today.
required_mobile_tests: pregnancy is presented for female only and never for male or unknown
age and medical-condition answers produce exactly the baseline tokens
body area produces no token and only filters the picker
impedance_mismatches.required_review: none — the predicate and token mappings are byte-identical

impedance_mismatches.baseline_behaviour: No skip mechanism exists anywhere in the follow-up flow. Every presented question must be answered; the only other exit is cancelling the assessment.
impedance_mismatches.candidate_behaviour: The schema supports `skippable` and a skip sentinel, but every projected question is skippable:false and no skip sentinel exists. The projection introduces no skip.
impedance_mismatches.why_it_exists: W3 requires optional skip logic to be expressible. Expressing it is not the same as using it, and using it on a clinical question is a decision no one has taken.
required_mobile_tests: no question is skippable in the shipped candidate
a required question can never be skipped
a skip sentinel, if ever added, produces no clinical token
impedance_mismatches.required_review: product + clinical, per question, before ANY question is marked skippable
impedance_mismatches.activation_blocker_reason: Nothing to activate: the projection contains zero skips.

im_001_deterministic_ordering.requires: regression evidence showing every changed tie path before production activation

im_002_immediate_red_flag_evaluation.implements: the existing locked architecture — red flags interrupt immediately and override scoring
does_not_authorize: adding or changing any red-flag token, rule or trigger
the rest of the adaptive engine
truncating a required red-flag question for convenience

question_wording.note: Preserving shipped wording is not an approval of it.
does_not_authorize: adding, removing or rewording any question

im_003_adaptive_re_branching.reason: Can change which symptoms a user declares, and therefore scoring inputs and the top condition. Not required for the IM-002 safety correction.
does_not_authorize: shipping re-branching alongside the IM-002 fix

_metadata.parity_claim: Behaviourally equivalent for question CONTENT, answer meaning and token effects. NOT identical for timing and determinism: see impedance_mismatches IM-001, IM-002 and IM-003, each of which is a deliberate, documented difference in a safe direction, not an accidental drift.
changelog: First versioned representation of the existing question flow.
No question added, removed or reworded; no answer meaning or token effect changed.
Declared deterministic tie-break replaces selection-order dependence (IM-001).
Red-flag-affecting questions declare immediate evaluation (IM-002) — specified, not yet implemented in Mobile.
Not published; may_publish is false and no clinical review is recorded.
provenance: Projected from wellapath-mobile a269168e2ed9b3b1c0453797dce5c9f303366854 by tools/build_question_candidate.py.
Every question, answer label and produced token is copied from the vendored Dart, not authored here.
No PHI and no real-user assessment data: this artifact contains only question definitions and token identifiers already published in token_dictionary 1.1.

path_controls.truncation_rule: After ordering, drop the lowest-priority questions until the follow-up count fits max_followup_questions. A question whose red_flag_evaluation.can_affect_red_flag is true is never dropped; if red-flag questions alone exceed the limit, the limit yields and all of them are asked.

proposed_options.rationale: Exactly today's implemented limit. Zero change.
Absorbs IM-003 adaptive re-branching without truncating; 3 clarifiers + severity + duration + additional + 1 headroom.
Keep 5 for ordinary questions, exempt red-flag questions entirely (already the schema constant).

path_controls.final_threshold_status: PENDING product and clinical approval — the values above are measured or proposed, not approved.
